body_markdown:
# BYD DOLPHIN SURF: Active, Boost or Comfort?

The most expensive DOLPHIN SURF in BYD’s European launch line-up is not the one with the longest published range. That distinction matters when a supplier offers “the top version” without explaining whether the buyer needs extra equipment, a stronger motor or more distance between charges. Active, Boost and Comfort answer different priorities, even though all three share a compact four-seat layout.

## Start with the European launch specification

The reference here is BYD’s European announcement dated 21 May 2025, supported by its European brochure identified as 0625-BPS-EN-V2. These are dated product references, not proof of a particular vehicle’s model year. A brochure date does not establish its production date, and a current stock listing does not automatically inherit the launch configuration. The figures below describe that European battery-electric hatchback line-up with front-wheel drive.

Keep DOLPHIN SURF separate from a quotation headed simply DOLPHIN. Nor should a seller substitute specifications for a Chinese-market Seagull or another market’s similarly named vehicle. Shared branding is not adequate evidence that batteries, equipment and documents match. Ask the supplier to identify the intended sales market, exact derivative and vehicle identification number (VIN), rather than approving the order from a familiar badge.

## What changes between the three versions?

The following values come from [BYD’s European launch announcement](https://www.byd.com/eu/news-list/BYD_brings_fun_future_ready_DOLPHIN_SURF_to_European_customers). Battery capacity is the manufacturer’s stated rated capacity; this table does not reclassify it as usable energy.

| European launch specification | Active | Boost | Comfort |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Battery capacity | 30 kWh | 43.2 kWh | 43.2 kWh |
| Motor power | 65 kW | 65 kW | 115 kW |
| Range, WLTP combined | 220 km | 322 km | 310 km |
| Maximum DC charging power | 65 kW | 85 kW | 85 kW |
| Three-phase AC charging power | 11 kW | 11 kW | 11 kW |
| Seats, including driver | 4 | 4 | 4 |

Active is the starting point to examine for a short, predictable daily route with dependable charging. Its smaller battery makes charging access particularly important to the decision. Do not approve it merely because a seller describes every SURF as having “up to 322 km” of range: that figure belongs to Boost in this comparison.

Boost combines the larger battery with the same stated motor power as Active. It is therefore the first version to compare when the purchasing priority is published combined-cycle range rather than maximum motor output. Comfort uses the larger battery too, but pairs it with the stronger motor and has a lower published WLTP combined range than Boost. A higher trim name is not a universal upgrade on every measurable attribute.

## Equipment can justify Comfort, but inspect the actual car

BYD’s launch description lists rear parking sensors and a reversing camera on Active. Boost adds electrically adjustable front seats, rain-sensing wipers and electrically folding mirrors. Comfort adds equipment including a 360-degree camera, LED headlights, heated front seats and wireless smartphone charging. These differences can be more useful to a particular user than the power increase alone.

For example, a buyer prioritising easier parking may value the camera system, while another with regular charging and short journeys may prefer to compare Active quotations. This is a purchasing judgment, not a road-test verdict. Request photographs and a demonstration of the quoted equipment. A generic image of Comfort should not serve as evidence for an Active shipment, and an equipment list copied from a different country should not settle a disputed feature.

## Four seats are a purchasing constraint, not a footnote

The launch specification lists four occupants, including the driver. If an operation needs five people in one car, none of these three versions meets that stated seating requirement. Resolve this before debating battery size or accessories. Do not treat the shape of the rear bench or a wide-angle cabin photograph as proof of another seating position.

BYD lists a 308-litre boot with the rear seats raised and 1,037 litres with them folded. The larger number is a different cabin arrangement, not luggage space available while all four occupants are seated. Buyers carrying equipment should compare their actual cases or luggage with the space and loading opening, not just rank cars by the largest published volume. Folding seats cannot solve a simultaneous requirement for rear passengers and that maximum cargo volume.

## Read charging figures as conditional capabilities

The distinction between 65 kW and 85 kW DC is worth preserving in the quotation. Neither number means that power is maintained throughout a charging session. BYD’s launch announcement quotes 30 minutes from 10% to 80% state of charge for all three versions. It is a manufacturer figure, not a promised stop duration at any public charger.

The [European brochure](https://www.byd.com/material/byd-site/eu/pdfs/dolphin-surf/Dolphin_surf-0625-BPS-EN-V2NEW.pdf) notes that battery temperature, charging infrastructure and state of charge affect charging. Its range notes also distinguish laboratory values from results influenced by weather, traffic, load and driving behaviour. Consequently, do not convert WLTP combined range into a guaranteed daily operating radius, or replace it with a city-cycle figure without changing the label.

Check the destination’s charging equipment, electrical supply and actual vehicle inlet together. Standard three-phase 11 kW AC capability does not prove that every premises can deliver it. Ask what cables are supplied and who will confirm compatibility. An independent [electrive report from May 2025](https://www.electrive.com/2025/05/30/first-ride-in-the-byd-dolphin-surf-riding-the-green-wave-to-the-red-light/) explicitly says its quoted DC charging time was not tested; repeating the number in a review does not make it a second measured result.

## Safety, software and after-sales need separate evidence

The [2025 Euro NCAP assessment](https://www.euroncap.com/assessments/byd/dolphin-surf/1209/) names a left-hand-drive DOLPHIN SURF. It reports a stable compartment in the frontal-offset test but also marginal rear-passenger chest protection in the full-width test. Read the detailed assessment and its applicability, rather than treating a headline as a guarantee of every situation or every imported derivative. A model-level assessment cannot establish the condition of a particular used car.

The European brochure also warns that navigation is not available in every language or country. Verify destination operation of connected services and obtain written warranty and repair-support terms from the responsible provider. European marketing materials alone do not confirm that those services follow a privately exported vehicle. This comparison makes no current price, stock, import-eligibility or registration promise.

## A decision worth putting in writing

Shortlist Active for a predictable route and reliable charging, Boost when the larger published range is the priority, and Comfort when its extra equipment and motor output meet a real need. Then reconcile that choice with the VIN, source-market specification, seating documents, equipment evidence and destination support. If a supplier combines Active’s name with Boost’s range or Comfort’s features, pause the purchase until the discrepancy is resolved in writing. Other model comparisons are available in the [vehicle catalogue](https://www.autobridgeexport.com/vehicles/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Comfort have the longest range?
No. In the cited European launch line-up, Boost is rated at 322 km WLTP combined, compared with Comfort’s 310 km and Active’s 220 km. Those figures are not guaranteed real-world distances.

### Does a 2025 announcement prove the vehicle is model year 2025?
No. The announcement identifies the reference configuration and date. The offered vehicle’s model year and production details need their own manufacturer or vehicle documentation.

### Can the SURF be ordered as a five-seater using this table?
No. All three cited European launch versions are specified for four occupants including the driver. Any different claim needs separate evidence for the actual vehicle, not an assumption from a related model.

### Is a quoted 30-minute charge a delivery promise?
No. It is BYD’s stated 10–80% DC figure under applicable conditions. Confirm the car, charger and operating conditions; do not turn it into a universal trip-planning guarantee.

Sources checked on 7 November 2026. This comparison is based on published documents, not a first-hand drive or vehicle inspection.
